title: Month 2 of Developing a Game with AI
author: Jealous-Street6221
selftext:
Hi everyone! I’m developing a game with the help of AI. Development started in February this year, and I began using AI as part of my workflow in July. I used to work as an INF programmer, and I’m currently developing the game full-time.

This is an open-world adventure game (AVG). You can explore different regions and cities, encounter all kinds of strange creatures, fight, and go on adventures. The game is being made with the Godot engine. At the moment, development is probably only around 10% complete, so some parts may still look a little rough. I’ll keep working hard to finish the game and make it as good as I can.

For coding, I used DeepSeek V4-Flash during the earlier stages of development, but I’ve now switched to GPT-5.6 Sol / 6 Sol. I haven’t used higher-end models such as Astra or Opus 5.5 because my budget is limited.

For the art, some assets are generated using Tripo and Hunyuan3D. These models still need to be brought into Blender for further polygon reduction and texture baking, which I do manually. Some other assets, such as buildings, are purchased from Fab. For animations, some come from Fab asset packs, while others are completely hand-keyed by me.

Overall, the AI workflow I use for this game is probably a fairly typical low-budget workflow. I also want to see whether it’s possible to make a solid game on a limited budget, because not every developer has access to flagship AI models. By the way, I spend around $20 per month on AI tools, which I think is already a relatively low cost for most people.

Finally, if you like the game, I’d love to hear any feedback, suggestions, or criticism! 😊Thank you, and I hope you have a wonderful day!

comments.author: amirati91
comments.body: Excellent work, only 10% complete and it looks very promising. You mentioned working with Tripo 3D and Hunyuan, how has the work been in creating the assets and making things look like they belong to the same world/artist?

replies.author: Jealous-Street6221
replies.body: Most of the time, I use gpt-Image or comfyUI running locally to generate multi-view reference images for the models first, and then use tripo or hunyuan for ai-based 3d modeling. This allows the models to use textures with a consistent visual style, as long as I keep the art style of the reference images consistent. I've also tried generating 3d models directly from text prompts, but the results weren't very good, and it was also difficult to maintain a consistent art style.

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
Hey! Alex here from the Tripo Studio US team. Really interesting breakdown of the workflow, especially keeping the whole AI stack around $20/month.

The Tripo/Hunyuan → Blender → poly reduction + texture baking pipeline stood out to me. For your Tripo assets, what usually takes the most manual work once you bring them into Blender: topology, polycount, textures, or something else?

comments.author: Afterlight_Games
comments.body: I'm building a game in Godot too, and the $20/month budget is honestly what caught my attention lol. Getting AI-generated assets to look consistent has been one of my bigger struggles. Between Tripo and Hunyuan3D, which one has given you better results after reducing polygons?

replies.author: Jealous-Street6221
replies.body: Tripo is better. Its built-in low-poly retopology works really well, and in most cases you barely need to do any additional cleanup yourself. Hunyuan’s current low-poly retopology tools are relatively weak, so I usually rely more on Blender’s built-in decimation tools to reduce the polygon count. I actually don’t use Tripo very often, because most of its features require payment. Hunyuan, on the other hand, gives you so much free quota every day that it’s almost impossible to use it all up. A big reason I can keep my monthly budget at around $20 is thanks to Hunyuan 😀.I’d recommend starting with Hunyuan to create your assets, then using Blender plugins such as Quad Remesher for cleanup and retopology. If the results are still poor, then consider switching to Tripo. This way, you can keep your costs as low as possible.
